target: Eu gosto de cozinhar para os amigos.
english: I like cooking for friends.
tip: Gostar always takes 'de' before what you like, so it is 'gosto de cozinhar' even though English 'like cooking' has no preposition.

target: Os vizinhos do andar de cima são barulhentos.
english: The upstairs neighbors are noisy.
tip: Andar means floor or storey here: o andar de cima = the floor above. The same word andar also means to walk.

target: Como ficou o bolo?
english: How did the cake turn out?
tip: 'Ficar' is used to describe how something turned out or ended up. 'Como ficou?' = How did it come out?

target: Quem vai levar as crianças?
english: Who's going to take the kids?
tip: 'Quem vai' = who will. 'Levar' = to take (someone somewhere). 'Buscar' = to pick up (the opposite).

target: Quando posso marcar a consulta?
english: When can I schedule the appointment?
tip: Marcar means to book or schedule: marcar a consulta = to make an appointment. Literally it means to mark.

target: Os documentos estão na pasta.
english: The documents are in the folder.
tip: Pasta means folder or briefcase, not the food: os documentos na pasta = the documents in the folder.

target: Como você conheceu a sua esposa?
english: How did you meet your wife?
tip: In the past, conhecer means to meet for the first time: conheceu = met. In the present it means to know.

target: Por que você escolheu essa carreira?
english: Why did you choose this career?
tip: In Brazil esse and essa often mean this, not just that: essa carreira = this career.

target: Quando você começou a trabalhar aqui?
english: When did you start working here?
tip: começar a + an infinitive means to start doing something: começou a trabalhar (started working).

target: Onde vocês vão passar as férias?
english: Where are you spending your vacation?
tip: passar means to spend time: passar as férias = to spend the vacation. Spending money uses gastar.

target: Por que não me avisaram antes?
english: Why didn't they tell me before?
tip: A they-form verb with no stated subject means they or someone in general: não me avisaram = they didn't tell me.

target: Eu moro no centro da cidade.
english: I live in the city center.
tip: 'No' is the contraction of 'em + o' (in the, masculine). 'Na' is 'em + a' (in the, feminine). Both are mandatory.

target: A noite está agradável para caminhar.
english: The evening is pleasant for walking.
tip: 'Noite' is feminine: a noite. Time periods: a manhã (morning), a tarde (afternoon), a noite (night). All feminine.

target: Eu preciso de ajuda com essa mudança.
english: I need help with this move.
tip: 'Precisar de' means 'to need.' The 'de' is required: 'preciso de ajuda,' not 'preciso ajuda.' However, before infinitives, many Brazilians drop the 'de.'

target: A televisão está na sala.
english: The TV is in the living room.
tip: Nouns ending in -ão are usually masculine: o avião, o coração, o limão. But some are feminine: a mão, a televisão, a estação.

target: O que você faz da vida?
english: What do you do for a living?
tip: 'Fazer da vida' is the everyday way to ask about someone's job, so 'O que você faz da vida?' asks what you do for a living.

target: Como se diz isso em português?
english: How do you say this in Portuguese?
tip: The impersonal 'se' in 'como se diz' means how does one say, with no specific subject, the normal way to ask for a word.

target: O que você acha dessa ideia?
english: What do you think of this idea?
tip: 'O que você acha de' is the go-to phrase for asking opinions in Brazilian Portuguese. Much more common than 'o que você pensa.'

target: Eu fui à praia com os amigos.
english: I went to the beach with friends.
tip: fui is the preterite of both ir and ser. Here fui à praia = I went; context tells the two apart.

target: O que você fez no fim de semana?
english: What did you do on the weekend?
tip: The weekend takes 'no': 'no fim de semana' = on the weekend. 'Fim de semana' is literally end of week.

target: Uma amiga minha trabalha nesse banco.
english: A friend of mine works at this bank.
tip: 'Nesse' is the contraction of 'em + esse' (in this). Other contractions: neste (em + este), naquele (em + aquele), nisso (em + isso).

target: O filme foi tão bom quanto o livro.
english: The movie was as good as the book.
tip: 'Tão + adjective + quanto' means 'as... as': 'tão bom quanto' = as good as. You can also use 'como' instead of 'quanto.'

target: Ela mora numa casa com um jardim grande.
english: She lives in a house with a big garden.
tip: 'Numa' is the contraction of 'em + uma' (in a, feminine). 'Num' = 'em + um' (masculine). Very common in speech.

target: Eu gosto das músicas brasileiras.
english: I like Brazilian songs.
tip: A definite article makes it specific: gosto das músicas (those songs) vs gosto de música (music in general).

target: A mão dele está machucada.
english: His hand is injured.
tip: 'Mão' is one of the few -ão nouns that is feminine: a mão. Its plural is 'as mãos.'

target: O sistema do computador travou.
english: The computer system froze.
tip: 'Sistema' is masculine (o sistema) despite ending in -a. Words of Greek origin ending in -ma are usually masculine: o tema, o cinema, o diploma.

target: Vocês precisam de alguma coisa?
english: Do you need anything?
tip: 'Vocês' means you all but conjugates like 'they': vocês precisam, vocês gostam.

target: Eu prefiro água com gás.
english: I prefer sparkling water.
tip: 'Com gás' = sparkling water, 'sem gás' = still. You order água com gás or água sem gás.

target: Ela gosta de tirar fotos.
english: She likes taking photos.
tip: 'Tirar foto' is the fixed phrase for taking a photo; tirar on its own means to pull or remove.

target: A gente precisa de mais espaço.
english: We need more space.
tip: 'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: a gente precisa, never 'a gente precisamos.'
